methods.label: Insert the required parentheses
methods.explanation:
The stated right-to-left rule makes \(c+d\) the first operation. Next, subtract that entire sum from \(b\), and finally divide \(a\) by the result. Thus the grouping is
\[
a\div\bigl[b-(c+d)\bigr].
\]
Subtracting the parenthesized sum changes both signs, so in ordinary notation this is
\[
\frac{a}{b-(c+d)}=\frac{a}{b-c-d}.
\]
The expression is defined when \(b-c-d\ne0\); otherwise the original division is also undefined. The answer is choice E.
